blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: Per this page, code needs a CRITICAL level next to StandardSeverity's constants, and `enum ExtendedSeverity extends StandardSeverity { CRITICAL }` does not compile. What does the page give as the fix?

options.text: Declare one interface and let both enums implement it
options.says: The page's fix is a common interface, such as Severity, that several enums implement, because an enum cannot extend another.

options.text: Create the extra constant at run time through the constructor
options.says: The page says enum constants are fixed at compile time: new on an enum is a compile error and reflective creation throws.

options.text: Declare ExtendedSeverity as a non-sealed subclass of the first
options.says: The page says an enum is implicitly final, or sealed when constants have bodies, so no subclass can add constants either way.

origin.section: Common Pitfalls and How to Avoid Them

questions.stem: An enum constant `RED` carries the fields `final int r, g, b`. Per this page, when `RED` is written by one JVM and read back by another, where do the read-back constant's field values come from?

options.text: From the stream, which carries each field of the constant beside its name
options.says: The page says these fields are not included in default enum serialization; only the name travels.

options.text: From a readObject method that the enum declares to restore its fields
options.says: The page says readObject, writeObject, readResolve and writeReplace are all ignored for enums.

options.text: From the receiving JVM's own constant, which is looked up by the name
options.says: The page says the receiving side gets its own constant, looked up by name(), with whatever field values that JVM has.

origin.section: Common Pitfalls and How to Avoid Them

concepts: An enum cannot extend a class or be extended, because it implicitly extends java.lang.Enum and is implicitly final or sealed.
Only an enum constant's name is serialized; the receiving JVM supplies its own constant with its own field values.
